cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg21.txt <<'EOF'
fix(streams): stream_filter_register released its frame, then released it again

Every `stream_filter_register()` call SIGSEGVs. Not on a stream, not through a filter, not with a
wrapper — on its own:

    class CustomFilter {}
    var_dump(stream_filter_register("custom.filter", "CustomFilter"));

php prints `bool(true)`; elephc dies with signal 11 before printing anything. Two of the three
exits restore x29/x30 and add 48 to sp, then branch to `__rt_sfr_ret`, which restores x29/x30 a
SECOND time — from `[sp, #0]` of a stack that by then belongs to the caller — and adds 48 again.
`ret` jumps to whatever those eight bytes happened to hold. x86_64 has the same shape: `leave` on
each exit, then `add rsp, 48` + `pop rbp` in the shared tail.

The shared epilogue is now the ONLY epilogue on both arches. Each exit sets its return value and
branches there; one place restores the frame, so there is no second place that can disagree with
it.

This was the whole user-filter cluster. `io::streams` goes from 42 failures to 14 — twenty-eight
tests, every one of them about buckets, brigades, PSFS return codes or `php_user_filter`
subclassing, none of which were ever reached: the program died at the registration that comes
first in every one of them. What looked like a missing filter engine was a helper returning to a
garbage address.

The narrowing is worth recording because it cost nothing. A segfault says nothing about where, and
the temptation is to open lldb. Eight variants of the SAME three lines said it first: the crash
survived removing the class body, the `var_dump`, the second registration and everything after the
call, and disappeared only when the call did. That named the helper before a single instruction was
read, and made the assembler a confirmation rather than a search.
EOF
